The '''2026 Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council election''' was held on 7 May 2026 to elect members of [[Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council]] in [[West Midlands (region)|West Midlands]], [[England]]. This will be on the same day as other [[2026 UK local elections|local elections]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Solihull Council Election Countdown 2026 {{!}} Every Seat. Every Ward. Your Vote. |url=https://www.solihullcouncilelectioncountdown2026.com/ |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=Solihull Council Election Countdown 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

== Background ==
In [[2024 Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council election|2024]], Conservatives retained control of the council.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Solihull result - Local Elections 2024 |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/election/2024/england/councils/E08000029 |access-date=2026-01-27 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenway |first=Sam |date=2024-05-03 |title=Solihull Council full election results as Conservatives buck national trend |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/news/midlands-news/solihull-council-full-election-results-29111328 |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=Birmingham Live |language=en}}</ref> During the term, four Conservative councillors left the party to formed an Independent group, of which three defected to [[Reform UK]] later on, In February, another Conservative councillor from the Shirley West ward defected to Reform UK.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenway |first=Sam |date=2026-02-25 |title=Solihull councillor makes move to Reform UK |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/news/midlands-news/fourth-solihull-tory-councillor-defects-33490332 |access-date=2026-04-27 |website=Birmingham Live |language=en}}</ref> 

In 2026, all 51 seats in the council across seventeen wards will be up for election due to ward boundary changes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Solihull local council elections {{!}} Solihull Metropolitan Borough Council |url=https://www.solihull.gov.uk/councillors-and-democracy/elections-and-voting/solihull-local-council-elections-may-2026 |access-date=2026-04-27 |website=www.solihull.gov.uk}}</ref> Several senior Conservative councillors, including former Leader of the Council Ian Courts, no longer stood for re-election in 2026. None of the three independent councillors prior to the election stood for re-election.
